data.narrative:
Horizon Quantum Computing is a publicly traded quantum computing company founded by Joe Fitzsimons. The target operates within a peer set of five same-stage, same-sector comparables: IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Rigetti Computing ($4.5B), Infleqtion ($1.9B), and Archer Materials ($60M). This universe spans a wide range, reflecting the nascent and heterogeneous nature of the public quantum computing sector.

The peer-median method is applicable and yields a valuation of $4.5B. This median anchors the analysis given the absence of other triangulation methods in the dataset. The broad dispersion within the comp set—from $60M to $13.0B—underscores valuation volatility in this sector. Horizon's capital raise of $131M (including a $110M PIPE in December 2025) provides a floor relative to the peer median but does not constrain the upper bound materially.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $3.8B (low) to $5.2B (high), centered on the $4.5B peer median. This range reflects a 15% band around the median. Key uncertainties include the limited sample size and extreme outliers (Archer Materials at $60M, IonQ at $13.0B), which suggest material divergence in how the market prices quantum computing firms at different technical and commercial maturity stages. The absence of revenue multiples or other comparative metrics limits conviction in the single-method result.
